 Rules that matter for correctness:
-- Select exactly the columns the question asks for, in the order asked. If the question asks for "details", "all information", or "which countries/students/items" without naming specific attributes, prefer returning the full rows of the relevant table(s) (e.g. SELECT T1.* or the joined tables' columns) rather than just a name.
-- String filters: stored values often differ from the question's wording in case, spacing, or suffixes. Unless you are certain of the exact stored value, match loosely: use LIKE '%keyword%' (drop trailing spaces/punctuation from the keyword) or = with COLLATE NOCASE. For a phrase like "includes the text 'X'", use LIKE '%X%'.
-- When several columns look plausible (e.g. an id vs. a name, student_id vs. friend_id, a code vs. a description), reason about which one actually holds the requested entity; for symmetric relations (friendship, matches), consider both directions only if the question implies it — otherwise use the column that identifies the subject of the question.
-- Use DISTINCT when the question asks for a set of entities and joins could duplicate rows.
+- Select exactly the columns the question asks for, in the order asked. If it explicitly names attributes (e.g. "first, middle and last names", "ids"), select exactly those.
+- Output shape for open-ended questions: if the question asks for "details", "all information", or simply "which countries/students/items ..." without naming specific attributes, and the relevant table holds many descriptive attributes, return the full rows (SELECT * over the joined tables, e.g. SELECT * FROM country T1 JOIN countrylanguage T2 ON ...), not just a name column. Prefer a narrow projection only when the question clearly wants just names/ids or the table has essentially only that column.
+- Duplicates: when you join a parent entity to a one-to-many child table (enrolments, registrations, memberships, languages, transactions), the same entity can appear once per matching child row. If the question asks about the entities themselves ("names of everybody enrolled in ...", "which students take ..."), use SELECT DISTINCT so each entity appears once. Do NOT deduplicate when the question asks for the individual records/events themselves ("list all enrolments", "how many times").
+- String filters: stored values often differ from the question's wording in case, spacing, or suffixes. Unless you are certain of the exact stored value, match loosely: LIKE '%keyword%' (drop trailing spaces/punctuation) or = with COLLATE NOCASE. For "includes the text 'X'", use LIKE '%X%'.
+- Symmetric relations (friendship, matches, sibling/peer links): a pair is usually stored once, in one direction only. To find entities that participate at all, consider BOTH id columns, e.g. WHERE ID IN (SELECT student_id FROM Friend UNION SELECT friend_id FROM Friend); for "no friends / never played", negate that union with NOT IN (filter NULLs) or NOT EXISTS checking both columns. Use a single direction only when the question explicitly refers to that role.
+- When several columns look plausible (an id vs. a name, a code vs. a description), reason about which one actually holds the requested entity.
 - For superlatives use ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1; include ties only if the question asks for them. Handle "not/no/without" with NOT IN / NOT EXISTS / EXCEPT, and beware NULLs inside NOT IN subqueries (filter them out or use NOT EXISTS).
 - Apply hints/evidence literally: use the given formulas, value mappings, and units exactly.
 - Only use tables/columns present in the schema; join through the foreign keys shown.
\ No newline at end of file

proposal.root_cause: Prompt rules actively push wrong semantics: anti-DISTINCT on fan-out joins, name-only projection for 'which X', and single-direction filters on symmetric relations
proposal.what: Rewrite system_prompt.md: (1) use SELECT DISTINCT when a 1:N join can repeat the requested entity unless individual event/enrolment records are asked; (2) for 'which <entities>' questions on attribute-rich tables return the full joined rows instead of only names; (3) for symmetric relations union both id columns before negation/aggregation. These target the exact error classes in sp0536, sp0755, sp0894 without touching control flow.

proposal.raw:
Diagnosis of the three failures: sp0536 is a join-fanout duplicate problem (gold dedups; prompt currently tells the model to avoid DISTINCT), sp0755 is an output-shape problem ("which countries" → gold returns full joined rows, not just names), sp0894 is a symmetric-relation direction problem (Friend stores one direction per pair; "has friends" must check both columns). All three are first-draft semantic errors that execute fine and return plausible non-empty results, so the existing repair loop never fires — the fix belongs in the generation rules. One edit: rewrite system_prompt.md with three targeted rules (dedup after 1:N joins unless enrolment/event records are asked; full-row projection for bare "which X" questions over entity tables with attributes; UNION both id columns for symmetric relations before NOT IN/NOT EXISTS).
